children: Sime Darby earnings visibility could remain clouded by softer demand in the Australasian mining sector, Affin Hwang IB analyst Afifah Ishak says in a note. Proposed U.S. taxes on companies investing in overseas data centers could slow investment in Malaysia and weigh on Sime Darby's efforts to diversify through its Caterpillar franchise, she says. Its Southeast Asian motor operations, excluding Malaysia, could partly cushion weaker performance in China and slower vehicle sales at its unit UMW amid intensifying competition. The analyst cuts Sime Darby's FY2027-FY2029 core EPS estimates by 21%-25% to factor in weaker margin assumptions across China Motors and Australasia Industrial. Affin Hwang downgrades the stock's rating to sell from hold and cuts target price to 1.80 ringgit from 2.43 ringgit. Shares are 1.4% lower at 2.07 ringgit. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
